issues.claim: "People who search the salon's name or follow an old link reach a for-sale notice instead of the salon." (audit_md, 'What it means for customers')
issues.problem: Unsupported, and contradicted by the audit's own cited source. A name search resolves to the Google Business Profile, whose website field and 'Book online' button both point to vagaro.com/villalonahairsalon (re-read today). Independent searches for 'Villalona Hair Salon North Brunswick NJ' and for 'site:villalonahairsalon.com' returned directory/Vagaro pages only, not the parked domain. links_to_broken_domain is empty and the auditor's own data_gaps say no public page still links to villalonahairsalon.com, so the 'old link' half has no traceable example either. This is the one sentence an owner is most likely to test, and it also contradicts the next sentence in the same paragraph.
issues.fix: Cut it to what is sourced, e.g. 'Anyone who still has the old address on a card, bookmark or old email lands on a for-sale page; searches and the Google listing go to Vagaro, so bookings are unaffected.' If an old link is found later, cite it.
